content.title: About
content.content: Brussels sprouts are small, cabbage‑like vegetables from the cruciferous family. Fresh sprouts are commonly steamed, boiled, or sautéed with added fat, which keeps them crisp and enhances their flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vegetable is named after Brussels, where it was first cultivated in the 16th century.
It is a rich source of vitamins C and K, as well as folate and dietary fiber.
More than 300 varieties exist, differing in size, leaf color, and taste.
Cooking with butter or olive oil improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
When stored properly in the refrigerator, sprouts stay fresh for 2‑3 weeks.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Compounds such as glucoraphanin and quercetin help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy gut function and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Provides beneficial phytochemicals
items.content: Sulforaphane, formed during cooking, may have anti‑cancer properties.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Brussels sprouts can cause increased gas in people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: High vitamin K content may affect the efficacy of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to cruciferous vegetables.

items.title: Added fat during cooking
items.content: Sautéing with a lot of oil significantly raises the calorie count.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Brussels sprouts can be steamed, boiled, roasted, or sautéed with a little oil. They pair well with garlic, lemon, balsamic vinegar, and nuts. Before cooking, trim the outer leaves and cut off the stem.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sprouts in the refrigerator in a plastic bag or container, keeping them dry. When stored correctly they stay fresh for 2‑3 weeks. Do not wash before storing to avoid excess moisture.
